content.user_title: Build Azure Event Hubs Python Streams
content.value_statement: Azure Event Hubs projects need reliable producer, consumer, and checkpoint patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused Python SDK guidance.
actual_capabilities: Shows installation commands for azure-eventhub, azure-identity, and blob checkpoint support.
Explains environment variables for Event Hubs namespace, hub name, storage URL, and checkpoint container.
Demonstrates EventHubProducerClient and EventHubConsumerClient setup with DefaultAzureCredential.
Provides batching patterns for sending events and handling batch size limits.
Covers partition IDs, partition keys, consumer starting positions, and Event Hub metadata lookup.
Shows synchronous and asynchronous consumer patterns with BlobCheckpointStore checkpointing.
limitations: Requires an existing Azure Event Hubs namespace, event hub, and permissions.
Does not provision Azure resources or create infrastructure templates.
Reference files and setup scripts are named, but only SKILL.md is present in this package.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted before production deployment.

use_cases.title: Prototype Stream Producers
use_cases.description: Create a Python producer that batches telemetry events and sends them through the Azure Event Hubs SDK.

use_cases.title: Build Reliable Consumers
use_cases.description: Implement a consumer with checkpoint storage so processing can resume safely after restarts.

use_cases.title: Review Partition Strategy
use_cases.description: Choose partition IDs, partition keys, and consumer starting positions for ordered event processing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Producer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help me create a basic Python Event Hubs producer with DefaultAzureCredential and batched sends.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Checkpointing Consumer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Python Event Hubs consumer that stores checkpoints in Azure Blob Storage after successful processing.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Partitions and Ordering
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my partition key strategy for ordered delivery and balanced Event Hubs consumption.

prompt_templates.title: Convert to Async Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to convert a synchronous Event Hubs producer and consumer plan into an async Python design.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for a Python producer that sends telemetry in batches.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan covering package installation, DefaultAzureCredential setup, batch creation, overflow handling, and context manager cleanup.

output_examples.input: A data engineer needs a restart-safe consumer for an Event Hub.
output_examples.output: A consumer design that uses BlobCheckpointStore, updates checkpoints after processing, and explains required storage settings.

output_examples.input: An architect wants guidance on Event Hubs partition choices.
output_examples.output: A comparison of partition IDs and partition keys with guidance for ordering, throughput, and consumer group behavior.

best_practices: Use managed identity or DefaultAzureCredential instead of embedding secrets in source code.
Checkpoint only after successful event processing to avoid losing unprocessed messages.
Use partition keys when related events must remain ordered within one partition.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode connection strings, account keys, or tenant secrets in examples or applications.
Do not checkpoint before processing finishes, because failed work may be skipped later.
Do not force all events into one partition unless ordering requirements justify the throughput limit.

faq.question: Does this skill install Azure packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It shows installation commands that a user can run when preparing a Python environment.

faq.question: Which authentication method does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes DefaultAzureCredential, which supports managed identity and local Azure developer credentials.

faq.question: Does it support checkpointing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows BlobCheckpointStore usage and explains updating checkpoints after event processing.

faq.question: Can it help with asynchronous clients?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async producer and consumer examples for higher-throughput Python applications.

faq.question: Does it create Azure Event Hubs resources?
faq.answer: No. The skill assumes the Azure namespace, event hub, storage account, and permissions already exist.

faq.question: Is the storage URL a fixed external endpoint?
faq.answer: No. The storage URL is a placeholder for the user-owned Azure Blob Storage account used for checkpoints.
